rows.text: Design-forward dog walking gear - harnesses, leashes, carriers, poop bag holders. Orders usually $60-120, mostly first-time puppy owners and urban millennials. Want to land new customers who just bought other pet stuff.
Natural supplements for dogs, mostly probiotics and hip/joint chews, around $35 a bag. Auto-ship is where we make our money, so anywhere that skews pet parents is great.
Modern cat trees, scratchers and wall-mounted furniture that doesn't look like a carpet-covered tower. AOV is about $150. We're after design-conscious apartment dwellers who own cats.
Self-cleaning litter box, $500-700. It's a considered purchase but people who already spend on pets convert well, and the 90-day trial helps. Prefer multi-cat households.
Monthly themed box of toys and treats for dogs, starts at about $23/mo with a 6 or 12 month plan. Looking for first-box signups from dog owners.
Hemp oil and chews for anxious or older dogs. Vet-recommended, 30-day guarantee. Not sure how ad networks handle the hemp thing so tell us what's allowed.
Soft, performance-y everyday clothing for guys and gals who want to go from gym to coffee. Joggers around $90, shorts $65. Want to reach people who've already shown they spend on activewear.
Lifting and training apparel for a 18-30 crowd. Leggings and tees in the $30-60 range; big on free shipping thresholds and first-order discount.
Cashmere sweaters for $50, silk for $60, that sort of thing. Basically luxury materials without the markup. Broad audience, women 30+ is our best segment.
Transparent-pricing wardrobe staples - tees, denim, work-appropriate pants. Our shopper is mid-career, cares about where stuff is made, spends $100-150 per order.
Merino wool and tree-fiber sneakers, $100-ish. Machine-washable. Looking for comfort-first shoppers, any age really.
Comfort socks and tees where every purchase donates an item to someone experiencing homelessness. Average order $65. Great for gifting and for families buying multi-packs.
Shapewear, loungewear and underwear, inclusive sizing XXS-5X. Mostly women 22-40 who buy on drops. Don't send us people who only shop discount.
Fair trade organic cotton underwear, tees and baby clothes. Affordable, around $30 an item. Eco-minded parents especially.
Running apparel with a heritage, New England feel - singlets from $58, jackets $200+. Our customer is a serious recreational marathoner, higher income, 30-55.
VIP membership gives women activewear at $25-50 per piece, billed monthly with skip option. We'd love to reach women in the market for workout clothes who haven't tried us.
Premium yoga and studio-to-street apparel. $80-130 per piece. Celebrity-adjacent aesthetic, so we want shoppers who care about brand and wellness.
Fewer, better things - leather totes, cashmere wraps, capsule wardrobe pieces. Orders $200-400. We want affluent women who've outgrown fast fashion.
Stylish clothing for women in sizes 00-40, with free exchanges within a year. Average order is about $140. Audience is women who've struggled to find quality in extended sizes.
Skincare and makeup for 'skin first' people, we're known for Boy Brow and Cloud Paint. Mostly 18-34 women, orders around $50.
Customized shampoo and conditioner built from a quiz - hair type, goals, scent. Subscription refills every 2 months. Looking for people who haven't found the right hair routine.
Custom skincare formulas from licensed providers, mostly acne and anti-aging. Free trial, just pay shipping. Needs a skincare-engaged audience.
Bond repair for damaged hair. Everyone should be using it lol. Salon and retail.
Fun, scent-forward hair care - dry shampoo, texture spray, body care. Orders usually $45-70. Young, social-media-native shoppers.
Prestige Japanese-inspired skincare - the Dewy Skin Cream is $72 and our hero. Typical order $110+. We think affluent women 30-55 who already buy premium beauty are the target.
Daily greens and nutrient powder, subscription at about $79 a month. Our target is health-conscious people who track habits and already buy supplements or work out regularly.
Traceable, minimalist multivitamins by subscription ($33-ish a month). We talk a lot about transparency. Looking at women 25-45.
Science-led daily probiotic subscription, about $50 a month. We want the evidence-focused wellness crowd, not impulse shoppers.
High-quality supplements used by pros and athletes - NSF Certified for Sport. Lots of SKUs, orders around $80. Prefer informed buyers over bargain hunters.
Supplements for skin, gut and energy. Think 'Daily Cleanse' and 'Red Carpet'. Bought as one-offs and subscriptions at $25-40.
Gummy vitamins - sleep, immunity, hair. Low price ($15-20) and we sell on playful flavors. Broad female audience 20-45.
Hydration packets you stir into water. Good for travel, workouts, hangovers. Our goal is trial.
High-protein, low-sugar kid-style cereal for adults. $39 for a 4-pack, subscribe and save. Looking for gym-goers and nostalgic millennials.
Squeeze-bottle olive oil for everyday cooking and finishing. Two bottles, about $20 for a combo. Home cooks, 25-40.
Sichuan chili crisp and other sauces, jars $15-20, gift sets for the holidays. Foodies, mostly urban and under 45.
Design-forward olive oils and vinegars from California; the Duo is $70 and it's one of the most gifted items we have. Higher income home cooks.
The world's strongest coffee, as advertised. Beans, grounds, cold brew cans. Our buyers are heavy coffee drinkers who like a bit of humor.
Matches you with fresh roasted bags from small roasters, subscription with a quiz. Bags run $15-25. Looking for home brewers and WFH folks.
Canned mountain water with a metal-heads attitude. Mostly sold in 12-24 packs. Young audience and anyone who likes edgy branding.
Prebiotic soda with 9g of fibre and low sugar, $36 for 12 cans. Skews health-conscious younger adults and parents swapping out regular soda.
Soda with apple cider vinegar and prebiotics, about $2.50 a can. Heavy Gen Z and Millennial skew, big on Instagram.
Membership grocery, annual fee about $60 for 25-30% off organic and non-GMO pantry goods. Perfect for families and health-minded shoppers who buy often.
Organic produce and pantry items delivered at up to 40% off supermarkets, weekly or biweekly boxes. We want budget-aware households who care about food waste.
Always Pan and other cookware in bright colors, $150ish for the Always Pan. Great for housewarming and wedding gifts, and for younger first-home buyers.
Ceramic non-stick cookware sets without PTFE. Sets are $400+. Women 28-45 who care about what their cookware is made of.
Professional-quality cookware and knives sold direct, used in restaurants. Pans start around $100, sets run $600 or more. Serious home cooks, mostly male.
Machine-washable rugs with a two-part system. Typical order $250-400. Great for pet owners and families with young kids who have messes.
Clean-ish everyday essentials - soap, toothpaste, pantry stuff, all on a $59 membership. For frugal minimalist households.
Meal kits starting around $8 a serving, new customer discounts big. We want busy families and young professionals. Weekly subscription.
Fully prepared meals that go from fridge to plate in 2 minutes. $11-14 per meal, weekly subscription. Targeting busy professionals and fitness folks.
Plant-based frozen smoothies, bowls and soups. 9-24 items per box. Wellness-minded women 25-45.
Gift baskets, pears, and holiday food gifts, $40-150. Q4 is basically our whole year. Looking for people who give gifts (corporate, family, hosts).
Flower bouquets delivered to your door, $55-100. Occasion-driven - birthdays, anniversaries, Mother's Day. Same or next day matters a lot to us.
Unique gifts from independent makers; lots of personalized stuff. Average order $85. Gift-givers with some budget, around birthdays and holidays.
We pick groceries and recipes for you based on a quiz, weekly box, around $90 a week. Targeting busy people who want to eat healthier without planning.
Fast chargers, power banks, cables. Mostly $20-60 purchases. We want phone-and-laptop users, and I'd say everyone qualifies.
Mattresses and bedding, 100-night trial, free shipping and returns. Mattresses run $600-2,000. It's a once-every-8-years purchase so we want people who just moved or are renovating.
Carry-on and checked suitcases, $275-$450, lifetime warranty. Frequent flyers and gift-givers, with the highest intent in spring and before the holidays.
Everyday 14k gold jewelry at $50-400. Lots of gifting. Women 22-40 who buy jewelry for themselves.
Mid-century modern furniture shipped direct. Sofas cost around $1,000-2,000 and delivery takes a couple of weeks. People in new homes or apartments.
Screen-free audio boxes for kids 3-8 that play stories when you place a character figure on top. Figures cost $15-20, speaker is $100.
Sleep devices: sunrise alarm clock, sound machine, and the Rest for kids' bedtime routine. $70-170. Parents and sleep-optimizers.
Interactive math, science and CS courses on mobile and web. Subscription is roughly $25/mo or $120/yr. Curious adults and students who like to learn in small chunks.
Annual subscription (~$120-180) to video classes from famous experts. Big gifting spike in Q4. We want curious, higher-income learners.
Banking app with no monthly fees and early direct deposit. Mainly younger and mid-income Americans, with a goal of account signups. Needs to comply with financial advertising rules.
Renters and pet insurance starting at about $5 a month, all by app. Looking for new renters and pet owners who just got a pet.
Low-sugar, lab-tested natural wines shipped monthly. $160-ish a box. Adults 21+ who care about wellness. Ship to states we're licensed in only.
Hemp-extract CBD gummies, oil and creams. $40-90 a bottle. Stress, sleep, exercise recovery. Need to know any platform restrictions.
Prescription glasses starting at $95 including lenses, free home try-on of 5 frames. Anyone who wears glasses or just got a new prescription.
Colorful outdoor gear - packs, jackets, duffels - from a certified B Corp. Lots of 'Del Dia' one-of-a-kind items. Orders $90-250.
Custom-fit floor liners and cargo mats, made in USA. Sets are $150-250. Targeting people who just bought a new vehicle.
Dating app 'designed to be deleted'. Free to download, premium tiers exist. Singles 22-38 in big US metros.
Documentary streaming from $4.99/month. Older, intellectually-curious audiences, science and nature fans.
Colorful, gender-neutral basics for babies and kids. Pieces are $12-30. Parents of kids 0-12 who like bundles and hand-me-down-able clothing.
Razors, blades, shaving cream and body wash for men. Starter set $15. Men 20-40 who are sick of overpriced drugstore cartridges.
Subscription play kits for babies and toddlers, designed with child development specialists. $80-ish a kit every few months. First-time parents.
Online bookstore that supports independent bookstores. Typical basket $30. Book lovers who'd rather skip Amazon.
Mattresses, pillows and seat cushions with a patented grid design. $1,000+ for a mattress. Back-pain sufferers and sleepers who run hot.
Wireless speakers and soundbars, $120-$900. Home audio fans, new home owners, tech-forward households.
Slim leather wallets and everyday carry bags, $80-200. A common gift for fathers and grads.
Video doorbells and security cameras starting at $60. New homeowners, renters, package-theft worriers.
Organic cotton family pajamas and kids' clothing, $40-70 per piece. Matching-family holiday pajama sets are our big seller. Parents, grandparents.
Subscription razors and grooming for men, from about $5 a month. Looking to reach men who haven't tried a razor subscription.
Connected bikes and treadmills ($1,500+) plus an app membership for $12-44 a month. Looking for people in the market for home workout.
E-readers, $100-$200. For avid readers, travelers, and as gifts.
Payroll, benefits and HR software for small businesses. We want owners and operators of companies with 1-100 employees, and the goal is demo bookings.
CRM software for marketing and sales teams, with a free tier. Our buyers are marketers at growing companies.
Customer support helpdesk built for Shopify merchants. Our audience is literally ecommerce store owners and ops leads - not shoppers - so we thought your merchants might fit?
All-in-one HR and IT for companies. Want leads.
Email marketing platform. Free plan, paid starting around $13. Small businesses and creators who sell online.

rows.category: local service - dentist, single location, Portland OR
rows.text: Family dental office in SE Portland, accepting new patients. We'd like to bring in locals for cleanings and exams. Only people within about 10 miles are any use to us.
Family plumbing and drain company in Columbus, Ohio. Water heaters, drain cleaning, repairs. Obviously only Columbus area folks matter.
Non-profit working to end the killing of dogs and cats in shelters. We're looking for monthly donors, ideally pet owners who care about adoption. Would a donation ask work at checkout?
We fund clean water projects in developing countries. Looking to turn thank-you page visitors into small recurring donors. $20 a month is our typical gift.
Sports betting and daily fantasy for adults 21+ in states where it's legal. Goal is first-deposit signups, and we have a big new-user promo. Regulated category.
Firearms, ammo and accessories retail. Customers must be 18/21+ and ship to an FFL for guns. Looking for outdoor/hunting audiences.
Online visits and prescriptions for things like hair loss and ED, plus skincare. Men 25-50 mostly. Rx products have extra ad rules obviously.
Donation platform used by Democratic campaigns and causes. Want to get small-dollar donors to give to candidates before the quarter-end deadline.
Natural toothpaste and deodorant, you know the stuff. Just show it to whoever. Cheap, like $5 or so.
blenders!! high powered, ppl love them. also commercial but mainly home. promo going on til friday i think
